lines.trans: Mateo, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!
Loud and clear. Are you beside the little stone fountain?
Yes! There are two small streets on the left: which one do I take?
Take the second street, beside the flower stall, not the narrow alley.
Walking now... oh, I see the golden key sign and the blue door!
Good! Is the metal shutter open?
He is opening it right now! Stay on the line one second.
Make sure the inner brass ring measures twenty millimetres.
He measured it against the old one: he has two left on the shelf!
Buy both! A spare valve saves next winter too.
Paid in cash! Keep your toolbox open, I am running back across the bridge!
Hurry up, I just heard footsteps on the second-floor stairs!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.
Yesterday we opened the shop early.

acabar.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)

meanings.en: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
meanings.note: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.

examples.trans: I have just arrived from the market.

examples.text: Ya acabamos el trabajo de hoy.
examples.trans: We already finished today's work.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.trans: I am heading there right now.
Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Alto y claro means 'loud and clear'.

examples.trans: It is a tall piece.

examples.text: Alto y claro. ¿Estás junto a la fuentecita de piedra?
examples.trans: Loud and clear. Are you beside the little stone fountain?

meanings.note: A finger ring or a circular metal fitting.

examples.trans: The ring is here.

examples.text: Vemos los anillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rings from the door.

asegurar.gloss: to make sure (asegurarse de); to secure

meanings.en: to make sure (asegurarse de); to secure
meanings.note: Asegúrate de que... means 'make sure that...'.

examples.text: Asegúrate de cerrar bien la verja.
examples.trans: Make sure you close the gate properly.

examples.text: El técnico aseguró que todo funciona.
examples.trans: The technician assured us everything works.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.
The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Caja de herramientas = toolbox; la caja also means the cash register/box.

examples.trans: The box is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cajas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the boxs from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Plural callejones.

examples.trans: The alley is here.

examples.text: Vemos los callejones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the alleys from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Camino veinte minutos hasta el centro.
examples.trans: I walk twenty minutes to the city centre.
We walk slowly across the bridge.

meanings.note: Shopfront sign or notice board.

examples.trans: The sign is here.

examples.text: Vemos los carteles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the signs from the door.

meanings.note: Alto y claro = loud and clear; ¡Claro! / ¡Pues claro! = Of course!

examples.text: El mensaje es alto y claro.
examples.trans: The message is loud and clear.
Well of course you can come in!

coger.gloss: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)

meanings.en: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)
meanings.note: Standard everyday Peninsula Spanish verb for picking up objects or taking transport (g -> j before o: cojo).

examples.trans: I take the bus every morning.

examples.text: Coge una taza limpia del estante.
examples.trans: Take a clean cup from the shelf.

colgar.gloss: to hang; to hang up (the phone)

meanings.en: to hang; to hang up (the phone)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuelgo) and g -> gu in preterite 1st sg (colgué).

examples.text: Cuelgo el abrigo detrás de la puerta.
examples.trans: I hang my coat behind the door.

examples.text: Colgó los farolillos entre las ramas.
examples.trans: He hung the lanterns among the branches.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Compro pan caliente en la esquina.
examples.trans: I buy warm bread on the corner.
Yesterday we bought six yellow lemons.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Entrar/salir corriendo = to run in / run out.

examples.text: Corro para no perder el tren.
examples.trans: I run so I do not miss the train.

examples.text: Los niños corrieron hacia la fuente.
examples.trans: The children ran toward the fountain.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun choosing from options (plural: cuáles).

examples.trans: There are two streets: which one do I take?
Which one is your teacup?

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Describes gold colour or golden-brown baked crust.

examples.trans: It is a golden piece.

examples.text: El del papel dorado del estante de arriba. ¿Por qué?
examples.trans: The one in gold paper from the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Pagar en efectivo means 'to pay in cash'.

examples.text: El efectivo es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The cash is very important here.
We talk about the cash.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Often singular (la escalera) or plural (las escaleras) for a staircase.

examples.trans: The stairs is here.

examples.text: Vemos las escaleras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stairss from the door.

meanings.note: Wooden wall or cupboard shelf.

examples.trans: The shelf is here.

examples.text: Vemos los estantes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shelves from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Opposite of ancho (wide).

examples.trans: It is a narrow piece.

examples.text: Coge la segunda calle, junto al puesto de flores, no el callejón estrecho.
examples.trans: Take the second street, beside the flower stall, not the narrow alley.

meanings.note: Marked in Spain by a lit green cross.

examples.trans: The pharmacy is here.

examples.text: Vemos las farmacias desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pharmacys from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la flor, las flores.

examples.trans: The flower is here.

examples.text: Vemos las flores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the flowers from the door.

meanings.note: Diminutive of la fuente (fountain).

examples.trans: The little fountain is here.

examples.text: Vemos las fuentecitas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the little fountains from the door.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Caja de herramientas = toolbox.

examples.trans: The tool is here.

examples.text: Vemos las herramientas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tools from the door.

meanings.note: Plural interiores.

examples.trans: It is an inner piece.

examples.text: Asegúrate de que el anillo interior de latón mide veinte milímetros.
examples.trans: Make sure the inner brass ring measures twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Coldest season of the year.

examples.trans: The winter is here.

examples.text: Vemos los inviernos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the winters from the door.

meanings.note: A la izquierda = on/to the left.

examples.trans: The left is here.

examples.text: Vemos las izquierdas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lefts from the door.

meanings.note: Junto a + noun works like a preposition meaning 'beside / next to'.

examples.trans: Sit next to the window.
We work together at the guesthouse.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Yellow copper-zinc alloy used for keys, lamps, and valves.

examples.text: El latón es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The brass is very important here.
We talk about the brass.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.
Do you like the courtyard room?

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?
I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: mido, midió).

examples.text: Mido el ancho de la mesa nueva.
examples.trans: I measure the width of the new table.

examples.text: El carpintero midió la tabla dos veces.
examples.trans: The carpenter measured the plank twice.

meanings.note: La persiana metálica = the metal shop shutter.

examples.trans: It is a metal piece.
Good! Is the metal shutter open?

meanings.note: Veinte milímetros = twenty millimetres.

examples.trans: The millimetre is here.

examples.text: Vemos los milímetros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the millimetres from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.trans: We have the same job.
I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise or realization.

examples.trans: Oh, there is the blue door!

examples.text: Oh, perdona, no te había visto.
examples.trans: Oh, sorry, I had not seen you.

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from pagar.

examples.trans: It is a paid piece.

examples.text: ¡Pagado en efectivo! Deja abierta tu caja de herramientas, ¡vuelvo corriendo por el puente!
examples.trans: Paid in cash! Keep your toolbox open, I am running back across the bridge!

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: Oír pasos = to hear footsteps.

examples.trans: The footstep is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pasos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the footsteps from the door.

meanings.note: Hermano pequeño = younger brother; de pequeño = as a child.

examples.trans: It is a small piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

meanings.note: Window blind or rolling metal shopfront shutter.

examples.trans: The roller shutter is here.

examples.text: Vemos las persianas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the roller shutters from the door.

meanings.note: De piedra = made of stone.

examples.trans: The stone is here.

examples.text: Vemos las piedras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stones from the door.

meanings.note: Planta baja = ground floor; primera planta = first floor; also a green plant.

examples.trans: The floor / storey is here.

examples.text: Vemos las plantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the floor / storeys from the door.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Tener prisa = be in a rush; ¡Date prisa! = Hurry up!

examples.trans: The hurry is here.

examples.text: Vemos las prisas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hurrys from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

meanings.note: El próximo invierno = next winter.

examples.trans: It is a next piece.

examples.text: ¡Compra las dos! Una válvula de repuesto salva también el próximo invierno.
examples.trans: Buy both! A spare valve saves next winter too.

meanings.note: Masculine noun in Spanish: el puente de piedra.

examples.trans: The bridge is here.

examples.text: Vemos los puentes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bridges from the door.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Puesto de flores = flower stall.

examples.trans: The market stall is here.

examples.text: Vemos los puestos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the market stalls from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

meanings.note: Una válvula de repuesto = a spare valve.

examples.trans: The spare part is here.

examples.text: Vemos los repuestos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the spare parts from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Un paraguas a tiempo salva el paseo.
examples.trans: A timely umbrella saves the walk.

examples.text: Tu idea rápida salvó todo el desayuno.
examples.trans: Your quick idea saved the whole breakfast.

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Positive counterpart of tampoco.

examples.text: Yo también quiero un trozo de bizcocho.
examples.trans: I want a piece of sponge cake too.
We also have mint tea.

meanings.note: Unaccented possessive (tu llave / tus llaves), distinct from accented pronoun tú.

examples.trans: Where is your toolbox?
I recognized your handwriting right away.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.trans: It measures exactly twenty millimetres.
It is eleven twenty.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.
See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is a green piece.

examples.text: Mateo, ¿me oyes? ¡Acabo de pasar la farmacia verde!
examples.trans: Mateo, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

volver.gloss: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)

meanings.en: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: vuelvo), past participle vuelto; volverse + adj = become.

examples.trans: I will be back in five minutes.
He smiled again right away.

meanings.note: Válvula de latón = brass valve.

examples.trans: The valve is here.

examples.text: Vemos las válvulas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the valves from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.
Coming right now with the keys!
